title: The Support Reply
intro: You posted that your Hedrio wallet will not show your coins. Someone replied.
This time you can talk back. Pick your replies and sniff each message as it arrives.
Every chat ends with your choice. Choose wisely.

notify.text: Sorry about your wallet! We can fix it in DMs…

banner: Message request · you do not follow this account

msg.text: Hi! So sorry your balance is not showing 😔

msg: . Our team can fix it right here in DMs.
Scan this to re-connect your wallet:

replies.text: Are you really Hedrio? How can I check?

msg: on every pop-up, and your coins reappear.

replies.text: Why would a fix need me to approve things?

msg.text: Your wallet could be locked in 10 minutes

replies.text: OK, I do not want it locked

dmfirst.label: They messaged first
dmfirst.lens: You never contacted this account. It found your public post and messaged you.
dmfirst.why: Real wallet teams do not hunt for people in DMs. Scammers watch public complaints.

link.label: Look-alike link
link.lens: This goes to hedrio-reconnect.help, not to Hedrio's real site.
link.why: A wallet "reconnect" page can ask your wallet to sign away your coins. Check where a link really goes.

approve.label: "Approve every pop-up"
approve.lens: Approvals and signatures can hand a stranger control of your coins.
approve.why: A real fix never needs you to approve things you cannot read.

rush.label: Pressure to hurry
rush.lens: A wallet "locked in 10 minutes" is a made-up deadline.
rush.why: Rushing you stops you from checking.

rename.label: Name changed on the spot
rename.lens: It renamed itself "official" when you asked.
rename.why: Anyone can change a display name in a second. That is not proof.

everyone.label: "Hundreds did it"
everyone.lens: It claims a crowd did it. You cannot check that.
everyone.why: Fake crowds are an old trick to make a risky thing seem normal.

hello.label: Friendly greeting
hello.why: Scammers are friendly. Kindness is not proof.

logo.label: Hedrio paw logo
logo.lens: A copy of the wallet's paw print.

actions.label: Use the help page inside Hedrio's own app

block_report.line: Blocked and reported. The fake support account was removed before it reached anyone else.

verify.line: Hedrio's own help page said: "We never message first and never ask you to approve connections in DMs." Case cracked.

go_ahead.line: The pop-ups gave a stranger permission to move your coins. The wallet was empty in minutes.

what_if.go_ahead: Asking "why does a fix need approvals?" was the way out. The answer is: it never does.
what_if.verify: Checking was smart. Reporting the account as well gets it removed faster.

golden_rule: Wallet support never messages you first. Never scan, connect or approve anything a stranger sends.

quick_check.q: A "wallet support" account messages you first and asks you to scan a code and approve every pop-up. What do you do?

options.text: Scan and approve, they are helping
Do not scan. Block, report, and use the help page inside the wallet app
Ask them to approve it for you

quick_check.explain: Approving unknown pop-ups can hand over your coins. Real wallet support never messages first.

hints.nudge: Why would fixing a balance need approvals?

rows.v: Replies inside the app, never in surprise DMs
Hand over control of your coins
